claim_checks.claim: The note Abstract reproduces the current publisher abstract and the research questions paraphrase its stated aims.
Status exchange is represented as one sender conferring status on a receiver, who compares actual with expected conferral and returns signed feedback; this feedback is stored in sender memory.
claim_checks.result: PARTIAL: direction and storage are supported, but the note’s claim of a source-level “tension” between the abstract’s reciprocal-exchange framing and the §11.3 sequence is unsupported. In §11.3 the receiver returns signed feedback to the sender after receiving status, so the described interaction can itself be reciprocal; the source provides no contradiction here.

claim_checks.claim: Satisfaction is based on recency-weighted positive feedback; memory can persist/reset; learning changes individualism; exiting is probabilistic and depends on satisfaction/individualism.
claim_checks.result: PASS at prose level; the source itself omits numerical formulas for weights, normalization, learning and exit.

claim_checks.claim: Experiment setup and reported group cohesion effects.
claim_checks.result: PASS at summarized level: FC and PA × NoMemory/Memory/Memory+Learning; membership persistence rises with memory; group existence declines under memory in FC but increases with Memory+Learning in PA; satisfaction is broadly similar; group-size/status outcomes are included in source.

claim_checks.claim: Model state faithfully represents the mechanism.
claim_checks.result: FAIL: Agent has only `feedback: [-1 | 1]` and World has a reset flag, but no feedback-memory sequence/container or per-agent memory-length state. §11.3 explicitly stores and recalls historical feedback with recency weights (and Table 11.1 specifies memory length 1–10, initial value 5). `MEMORY_LENGTH = 5` alone does not represent the retained history, and the type therefore leaves the defining memory mechanism under-specified.

GAP: publisher chapter states that the original version was revised and links a correction chapter dated 06 May 2026. The correction landing page could not be opened; this audit cannot establish whether correction affects the extracted model, tables or results.

claim_checks.claim: A source-level conflict exists between the abstract’s “reciprocal exchanges” and the detailed interaction sequence.
claim_checks.result: FAIL: this interpretation is not justified; returning feedback is a reciprocal response to status conferral. The note should explain the ordered interaction directly and remove the claimed tension.

warning_status: No note edits; source note warning remains audit failed.
reason_for_fail: The typed state omits the explicit feedback-history container/range despite memory being defining; the note also asserts an unsupported source conflict about reciprocal exchange. Correction history is additionally linked on the current publisher page but its separate chapter was unavailable to inspect.
